resources.string: Walk a distance you know, and Passo works out the length of your step from it.
No GPS: the step counter counts the steps, you give the distance. Every distance and calorie estimate rests on this length.
A running track is %1$s around its inside lane, a football pitch about %2$s long. The longer the walk, the better the measure.
Stand at the start and tap Start.
Walk to the finish at your everyday pace. The phone can stay in your pocket: every step is counted.
Run to the finish at your usual pace. The phone can stay in your pocket: every step is counted.
At the finish, take the phone out and tap Stop.
Waiting for the step counter. If it takes long, take a few steps and come back to the start.
Passo can’t read the step counter
Measuring your step needs the physical activity permission, the one Passo counts with.
The phone can stay in your pocket: the steps are counted all the same, and show here when you look.
%1$s is a run. To measure your walking step, walk the distance at your everyday pace.
%1$s is a walk: Passo uses the running step only for minutes at %2$s or more.
Today’s distance and calories follow the new step. Past days keep theirs, unless you apply the profile to them in Settings.
